In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah As-Saffat

It is a Meccan surah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By those who range themselves in ranks, rank upon rank﴾. Masruq related from Ibn Mas'ud, and Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, that they are the angels. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas that they are the inhabitants of the heaven.

It is also reported from some of them that what is meant is the rows of the Muslims in congregational prayers. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Will you not form rows as the angels form rows before their Lord?"

The most well-known of the opinions is the first, namely that the angels are ranks in the heaven, remembering Allah exalted is He, and He remembers them. It is also said that the meaning of the verse is that the angels spread out their wings when they descend to the earth.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿By those who drive away with a driving﴾. Most of the exegetes held that what is meant by them is the angels, who drive the clouds so that they move them to the place that Allah the Exalted wills.

The second view: they are the admonitions of the Qur'an.

Regarding His saying: ﴿By those who recite the remembrance﴾, most of them held that what is meant by them are the angels, who recite the remembrance of God.

The second view: they are the prophets, who recite what God Most High has sent down. The third view: they are the verses of the Qur'an, which are recited for the remembrance of God Most High.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ — this is the place of the oath. So God, exalted is He, swears by what was mentioned before. And His saying: ﴿By those who line up in ranks﴾ means: "And by the Lord of those who line up in ranks," and so it is with what follows.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾. The meaning of the verse is that your God is One, and He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾, i.e., and Lord of the easts and the wests (al-masarib).

If it is said: He has said elsewhere ﴿Lord of the East and the West﴾, and He said elsewhere: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾, and He said here: ﴿Lord of the easts﴾. So how is the reconciliation of this verse with its counterparts?

The answer to this: as for His saying ﴿Lord of the East and the West﴾, what is meant by it is the direction; the East has one direction and the West has one direction.

As for His saying ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾, what is meant by the two easts is the east of winter and the east of summer. As for His saying ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾, the sun has easts from which it rises each day, from an east other than the east from which it rose yesterday, and likewise the wests. Thus the aspects of the verses are harmonized by this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 6:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars﴾. That is: with the beauty of the stars and their light. ʿĀṣim recited "bi-zīnati al-kawākib" (with the adornment of the stars), meaning: by Our adorning the stars. Ḥamzah recited "bi-zīnati al-kawākib" with the letter bāʾ in the genitive case (bi-khafḍ al-bāʾ) and the word zīnah with tanwīn (nunation). In this reading, al-kawākib (the stars) serves as an explanation of the adornment (zīnah), and the meaning is: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the stars.

And His saying: ﴿And as a protection﴾, meaning: and We protected them with protection. And His saying: ﴿from every rebellious devil﴾, meaning: rebellious (mārid, "defiant"). The shayṭān (devil) is every rebellious, insolent one, whether from mankind, from the jinn, or from the beasts. The poet said:

(Mā laylatu al-qufayr illā shayṭān ...)

And al-qufayr (the well) is the well that is deep in its bottom.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 8:

His words ﴿They cannot listen﴾ — it is also read as "لَا يسمعُونَ" with a fatha on the sin (lā yassammaʿūna, with the sīn doubled and vowelled with fatḥa), and his words ﴿They cannot listen﴾ mean: they do not listen (lā yastamiʿūn), and his words ﴿They cannot listen﴾ mean: they do not listen (lā yastamiʿūn).

And his words ﴿to the Highest Assembly﴾ mean: the angels, and the meaning of the verse is that they are unable to listen to the Highest Assembly.

And his words ﴿and they are pelted﴾ mean: they are stoned (yurjamūn), and his words ﴿from every side﴾ mean: from the sides of the heaven.

And His saying: ﴿dahūran﴾ (repelled). Mujahid said: that is, driven away. Qatadah said: they are pelted with projectiles. Al-dahr (driving away) is distancing, and it is said: Allah dahara-hu, that is, Allah removed him far away.

And His saying: ﴿wa-lahum ʿadhābun wāṣib﴾ (and for them is a punishment, enduring), that is, perpetual,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 10:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Except one who snatches a snatch﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: this is an exception of the disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "But whoever snatches a snatch." Al-khatf (snatching) is the seizing of something swiftly, and their snatching and seizing is the words of the angels.

And His words: ﴿So a piercing flame pursues him﴾. That is, a shining flame (shihab mudi'). It was said: a burning one (muhriq). And it is related from Yazid al-Raqashi that he said: "Thaqib" means that it pierces them, so it passes through to the other side. And al-shihab (the flame) here is the star.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 11:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So ask them﴾, that is: ask them, ﴿Are they more difficult to create, or those We have created?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and others said: what is meant is the heavens, the earth and the mountains. But the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) claimed that the angels and what God has created of the jinn and of the rational beings must necessarily be intended by the verse, because God the Exalted said ﴿or those We have created﴾, and "man" (man) is only mentioned for those who have reason.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We created them from clay that is sticky﴾, that is: adhesive (lasiq). Abu 'Ubayda said: it means lazim (firmly adhering). The poet said:

﴿And do not think that good will be without any evil after it... and do not think that evil is a blow that does not stick﴾

That is: lazim.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 12:

And His saying: ﴿Nay, but you wonder﴾. Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read "Bal ʿajibtu" (Nay, but I wonder), attributing the wonder (taʿajjub) to God. This is the reading of ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās.

In some transmitted reports from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, he said: "I was with Shurayḥ, and I recited 'Bal ʿajibta wa-yaskharūn' (Nay, but you wonder, and they mock). Shurayḥ said: 'How bad is this reading! God, exalted is He, does not wonder at anything, for He knows all things.' Shaqīq said: 'I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and Ibrāhīm said: "Shurayḥ is a man who is vain about his knowledge, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was more knowledgeable than him."'"

As for the reading with the fatḥah (nasb), it is addressed to the Prophet, and its meaning is: "Nay, but you wonder at Our revelation to you." It has also been said: "at their denial of you despite the clarity of the proofs."

And His saying: ﴿and they mock﴾, that is, they mock and ridicule you. As for the reading with a ḍammah on the tā' (ʿajibtu), the wonder attributed to God is not like the wonder of human beings, and God, exalted is He, has said in another place: ﴿So they mock them; God mocks them﴾ and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿God mocks them﴾. So the meaning of His saying ﴿ʿajibtu﴾ is: My forbearance regarding their sins is great. The one who wonders is one who sees something that is great in his estimation. It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿Nay, but I wonder﴾ is: their action has been placed in the position of what one wonders at.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Your Lord wonders at a young man who has no youthful lapse."

And it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Your Lord wonders at your despair and your quick answering of you [when you call upon Him]."
And His saying: ﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾ — and when they are admonished, they do not heed admonition.
And His saying: ﴿When they see a sign, they mock﴾ — that is, they mock (yaskharūn). It is said: some of them summon others to mockery (sukhriyyan).
﴿And they say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾ That is: clear magic.
Their saying: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again?﴾ They said this by way of denial.

Surah 37 (al-Saffat), verse 17 is "Or our forefathers of old?" Translating the commentary sentence:

And His saying: ﴿Or our forefathers of old?﴾ means: "Will we be resurrected, and will our forefathers of old be resurrected?"

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Yes, and you will be humbled.﴾ That is: "Yes, you will be resurrected." And His words ﴿and you will be humbled﴾ mean: abased and humiliated. The poet said:

((And there remains none but one who is humbled in a pen, and one who has fled into a hole, other than in your earth, into my hole))

Almighty God's saying: ﴿It will be but a single shout﴾, that is, one cry.

His saying: ﴿and behold, they will be looking on﴾, that is, waiting. It is also said: they will look at one another.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ That is: the Day of Reckoning and the Day of Requital.

This is the Tafsir of al-Sam'ani on Surah 37, verse 21.

His words, "Most High": ﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny﴾. That is, the Day of Judgment. It has also been said: it is the Day of Distinguishing between the one who does good and the one who does evil. And His words, ﴿which you used to deny﴾, mean: which you used to reject.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 22–23:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their companions﴾. Those who did wrong are the polytheists.

And His saying: ﴿and their companions﴾ means: and their likes (ashbahahum). It is also said: their associates (qurana'uhum). And it is said: their followers (atba'uhum).

And His saying: ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then guide them to the path of the Hellfire﴾, meaning: direct them to the way of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 22–23:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their companions﴾. Those who did wrong are the polytheists.

And His saying: ﴿and their companions﴾ means: and their likes (ashbahahum). It is also said: their associates (qurana'uhum). And it is said: their followers (atba'uhum).

And His saying: ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then guide them to the path of the Hellfire﴾, meaning: direct them to the way of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 24:

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿Stop them﴾. If it is said: How does He say, "Then guide them to the path of Hellfire" (fa-hdūhum ilā ṣirāṭ al-jaḥīm), and then say, "Stop them"? We say: Because they are made to stand upon the path (al-ṣirāṭ) for questioning. It is also said: this is more severe in punishment and rebuke. And in the report (khabar) from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that he said: "The feet of the children of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection until they are questioned about four things: about their youth, how they wore it out; and about their life, how they spent it; and about their wealth, from where they acquired it and where they spent it; and about their knowledge, what they did with it."

The statement of God Most High: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ That is, you do not help each other, so that some of you help others.

In the tafsir (exegetical reports) it is related that Abu Jahl was the one who said: "We are all victorious," as God Most High has recounted. God Most High then responded to his statement, ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ That is: let some of you help others today, if you are truthful.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, they will surrender today﴾. That is, they submit and bite their hands, and they know that there is no escape for them from destruction and punishment.

And they will turn to one another, questioning each other. (The phrase means: and they will blame one another.) Their statement, ﴿You used to come to us from the right side﴾, Al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and others among the scholars of meanings said: that is, from the direction of those who deceive us. It was also said: from the direction of Paradise, you would hinder us from it. Some of them mentioned that the leaders of the disbelievers used to swear to the followers that they were upon the truth.

Therefore His saying: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right⁠﴾ means: from the oaths by which you swore that you were truthful. "Al-yamin" (the right hand, here oath or strength) is mentioned and intended to mean strength. The poet said:

(When a banner is raised for glory... ʿUrāba meets it with the right hand)

That is: with strength.
His words, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ — that is, the leaders say this to the followers.
And His saying: ﴿And we had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people.﴾ That is: you did what you did by your own doing, and we did not do anything to you.

Divine saying, "So the word of our Lord has come true against us" (Q. 37:31): that is, the punishment of our Lord has become binding upon us. Al-Hasan said: the one who goes astray and the one who leads astray are both in the Fire. This is the meaning of His saying, "Indeed, we are tasting [the punishment]" (Q. 37:31): that is, we are tasting the punishment.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We misled you, for indeed we were ourselves misguided.﴾ That is: We led you astray, for indeed we ourselves were misguided.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 37, verse 33:

His saying: ﴿So on that Day, they will be sharers in the punishment﴾. He means: they will all be together in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals.﴾ The meaning is apparent, and the criminality (jurm) here is polytheism (shirk).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," would become arrogant﴾ toward the statement of tawhid (the declaration of Divine oneness), and they would refuse to utter it.
Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Are we really going to abandon our gods for a poet possessed?﴾ They said this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted responded to them, saying:
﴿Nay, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers.﴾ That is, the messengers who came before him in prophethood.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 38–39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 38–39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾. The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾. That is: those who were sincere in monotheism (tawhid).
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those, for them is a known provision﴾, meaning: determined, and their determined provision is their provision morning and evening,

Concerning His saying: ﴿Fruits, and they will be honoured﴾. "Fawakih" (fruits) is the plural of "fakihah" (fruit).

And His saying: ﴿and they will be honoured﴾, meaning: by their being admitted into the Garden.
In the Lord's words, ﴿In Gardens of Bliss﴾, meaning: they are in the Gardens of Bliss.
Their statement, "﴿On couches, facing one another﴾": the people of tafsir said: none of them looks at the nape of another's neck.
Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿They will be given rounds of a cup from a flowing spring﴾. That is: wine that is flowing.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The wine of Paradise is whiter than milk." Ibn Mas'ud recited: "yellow, delicious to the drinkers."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Neither will there be in it any intoxication﴾ means: it will not seize their minds (lit. "will not assassinate their intellects"). The poet said:

(So the cup has not ceased to seize us, and to fell with its first and its foremost.)

It is also said: wine is the ghoul (ghawl, a destroying calamity) of the intellect, and war is the ghoul of the soul. It is also said: al-ghawl is al-ghā'ila (ruin, harmful consequence), and among the ghā'ila is the loss of their reason, and all the other harms that are in wine. It is also said that there are four things in wine: intoxication (sukr), headache (ṣudā', ṣudā' meaning headache), vomiting (qay'), and urination (bawl), and none of these four is found in the wine of Paradise.

As for His saying: ﴿nor will they be made drunk by it﴾, it is said: anzafa al-rajul means the man became intoxicated, when he was drunk. The poet said:

(By my life, if you have become drunk or sober... wretched were the boon companions you were, O family of Abjar.)

Allah's saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, meaning: those who have restricted their glances to their husbands, that is, they have restrained their eyes, so they do not look at anyone other than their husbands.

And His saying: ﴿with beautiful, wide eyes﴾, meaning: beautiful of eyes. In the tafsir it is said: the whiteness is intensely white and the blackness is intensely black, meaning in the eye.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 49:

And His saying: ﴿As if they were eggs well-guarded﴾. The Arabs liken the complexion of a woman to the whiteness of an ostrich egg, and they say: the finest color is whiteness mixed with yellowness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

(Dark-eyed, in the white of her eyes a yellowish lustre, with deep black pupils; as if she were silver that gold has touched.)

And His saying: ﴿maknun﴾ means: concealed, guarded from the feathers (and the veil).

Some of them said: regarding His saying ﴿eggs well-guarded﴾, He likened them to the whiteness of the egg when it comes out of its shell. And it was said: He likened them to the membrane (al-simaha, the thin inner skin) that lies between the outer shell and the white.
Allah's words: ﴿Then some of them turned toward others, questioning one another﴾. That is, some of them ask each other about their condition in the world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 51:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿A speaker among them says: "Indeed, I had a companion."﴾ Mujahid said: "The qarin (companion) here is the Shaytan (Satan), who misguides him." It is also said: "The qarin here is his companion who used to invite him to disbelief."

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani said: "The verse was revealed concerning two men among the Children of Israel who acquired great wealth. It is also said: they inherited great wealth and divided it between them. One of them spent his share upon the poor, while the other bought with it estates and houses and became rich. These are the two whom Allah mentioned in Surat al-Kahf. Some of them said: they were two brothers other than those two."
"And His saying: ﴿He says, "Are you indeed among those who affirm?"﴾ That is: among those who affirm the Resurrection."

And His saying: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be held to account?﴾ This is the speech of his companion. His saying ﴿shall we indeed be held to account﴾ means: will we be called to reckoning (muhasabun). It is also said: will we be recompensed (mujzayun). It is said: "As you judge (tadin), so you will be judged (tudan)."

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿He said, "Would you like to look down?"﴾ Opinions differ regarding this. One of the two views is that Allah, exalted is He, says to them: ﴿Would you like to look down?﴾

The other is that this believer says to his brethren among the people of Paradise: "Would you like to look down?"

Allah's words: ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾. That is, in the middle of the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim). The middle of a thing is called sawa' (sawāʾ, "evenness, the middle") because its sides are equal (istiwa' al-jawanib) from it.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said: By Allah, you nearly brought me to ruin﴾. That is: "to destroy me." It is said: "kada yaf'alu kadhā" means he came close to doing so. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "in kidta latughwīnī" (indeed you nearly misled me), from al-ighwā' (leading astray).

Almost in the Quranic verse: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would certainly have been among those brought forward (to punishment).﴾

Translation of the commentary:

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would certainly have been among those brought forward﴾ mean: Had it not been for the mercy of my Lord, I would have been among those brought to the Fire, that is, those who entered the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 58–60:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Are we not to die, except for our first death, nor are we to be punished?﴾ It is said: "Answer us," but they do not answer, due to their being absorbed in the punishment. They say: ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾ And it is related from some of them that death will be brought in the form of a ram, and it will be slaughtered, as the report has come concerning it. Then they will say: ﴿Are we not to die, except for our first death?﴾ This is in the manner of acknowledgment, amazement, and joy at that.

For such as this let the workers work. That is: for the likes of this abode, and for the likes of this bliss, let those who work, work.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 62–64:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is that better as a welcome (nuzul), or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ The nuzul (welcome, hospitality) is the gift of the abode. It is also said: the nuzul is the provision prepared for those who are received (lit. upon whom it descends).

If it is asked: how can He say, ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ when there is no good at all in the tree of zaqqum?

The answer to this has already been given, and to similar questions. The Arabs say: "Come, let us see whether peace is better or war, poverty or wealth, health or sickness." What is intended is to establish the matter for the addressee, that there is no good except in one of the two.

As for His saying, ﴿or the tree of zaqqum﴾, the scholars differed concerning this tree. The majority hold that it is a tree whose like is not known in this world. Qutrub said: it is a bitter, foul tree that grows in Tihama. Some of them said: it is a deadly plant.

It is related in the exegesis that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Do you know what the zaqqum is?" Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari said: "Yes, we know it. In the language of the Berbers it is butter and dates." Some of them reported that it is in the language of Yemen. Abu Jahl then said to his slave-girl: "Bring us butter and dates." She brought them, and he said: "This is the zaqqum with which Muhammad (ﷺ) has frightened you," so they ate of it heartily (tazaqqamu). Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs up from the root of the Hellfire﴾, i.e., from the bottom of the Hellfire.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is that better as a welcome (nuzul), or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ The nuzul (welcome, hospitality) is the gift of the abode. It is also said: the nuzul is the provision prepared for those who are received (lit. upon whom it descends).

It is related in the exegesis that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Do you know what the zaqqum is?" Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari said: "Yes, we know it. In the language of the Berbers it is butter and dates." Some of them reported that it is in the language of Yemen. Abu Jahl then said to his slave-girl: "Bring us butter and dates." She brought them, and he said: "This is the zaqqum with which Muhammad (ﷺ) has frightened you," so they ate of it heartily (tazaqqamu). Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs up from the root of the Hellfire﴾, i.e., from the bottom of the Hellfire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 62–64:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is that better as a welcome (nuzul), or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ The nuzul (welcome, hospitality) is the gift of the abode. It is also said: the nuzul is the provision prepared for those who are received (lit. upon whom it descends).

If it is asked: how can He say, ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ when there is no good at all in the tree of zaqqum?

The Qur'anic verse "Its shoots are as if they were the heads of devils" (﴿طلعها كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوس الشَّيَاطِين﴾).

And His words: ﴿Its shoots are as if they were the heads of devils﴾. If it is said: how does He say ﴿Its shoots are as if they were the heads of devils﴾ when no one has seen the heads of devils, and description is not permissible except by means of something known?

The answer to this: it was firmly established in souls that the heads of devils are ugly, and that they all are in the most hideous form. So it was likened to them, according to what was firmly established in souls. The poet said:

(It fights me, while the Indian sword is my bed, and spears tipped with blue points like the fangs of ghouls.)

So it was likened to the fangs of ghouls, though one has not seen ghouls; but the comparison is valid because their ugliness is established in souls. Some of them said: the devil here is an ugly-looking snake, so its meaning is: as if they were the heads of snakes. The Arabs call every ugly, detestable thing a shayṭān (devil). Some of them said: it is the name of a plant of fruit, rough to the touch and foul in smell.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We have made them a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ (﴿إِنَّا جعلناهم فتْنَة للظالمين﴾). Their trial with it is what Abu Jahl said, claiming that it was butter and dates (al-Zabad wa-l-tamr). And among their trials with it is also that they said: how can a tree grow in the fire, when the fire burns trees?
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed they will eat from it, and they will fill their bellies with it﴾. The apparent meaning is clear.
And His saying: ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water﴾. That is: a mixture of boiling water.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 68:

And His saying: ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire (al-Jahim)﴾, meaning: their place of return. It is said: the tree of zaqqum (al-Zaqqum) is in the sixth gate of the gates of Hell; so they come out from the Hellfire to it, until they eat the zaqqum, then they are returned to the Hellfire. This is the meaning of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Then indeed your return is to the Hellfire﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 69:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾. That is: they found their fathers upon misguidance.
"And His saying: ﴿So they were hastening along in their footsteps﴾. That is, they hurry, and al-Ihra' (hastening, rushing) is al-Isra' (quick pace)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 71–73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And most of the former peoples had indeed gone astray before them. And We had certainly sent among them warners. So look at how was the end of those who were warned.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 71–73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And most of the former peoples had indeed gone astray before them. And We had certainly sent among them warners. So look at how was the end of those who were warned.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾. It is also recited as "mukhlisin" with a kasra on the lam. So His words ﴿mukhlasin﴾ mean: those whom Allah has purified and chosen. As for the reading with the kasra, it means: those who have made their deeds sincerely for Allah the Exalted.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Noah certainly called Us, and We are the best of those who answer.﴾ That is: We are the best answerer to him. He said "the answerers" (al-mujibun) in the plural as kings and great ones do, who speak of themselves with the plural form.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We delivered him and his family from the great distress﴾, i.e., the great grief,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 77:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾. We have already explained that mankind descends from the lineage of Noah, peace be upon him, and that no one remained from any lineage other than his.
And His saying: ﴿And We left for him among later generations﴾, meaning: We left for him, among the later generations, a good remembrance and a fine praise.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾. That is: safety belongs to him from us among the worlds. It is also said: the peace from us upon him among the worlds.
The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾ Its meaning is known.
The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾ Its meaning is known.
Then, ﴿We drowned the others﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and the mention of Noah has already preceded this.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed, among those of his party was Abraham﴾. It is said that the pronoun here refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), but the more correct view is that it refers back to Noah. The shi'ah (party, followers) are the adherents, and He said "among his party" only because Abraham was upon his path and method.

And His saying: ﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾. It means: sound, free from shirk (associating partners with God). ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: "He never cursed anything at all, so he understood the meaning of His saying: ﴿sound﴾."

Divine saying, the Exalted: ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾ Its meaning: "What thing is it that you worship?" It is a question in the form of denial and rebuke.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is it falsehood, gods other than God, that you desire?﴾ That is: you seek gods that are fabricated (mu'tafikah). The meaning of "you seek" is that you seek from them what is sought from God, exalted is He. Al-ifk (falsehood) means lying. The meaning of "mu'tafikah" is that you lied against God on their account, and you invented them from your own selves.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿[Is it falsehood, gods besides God, that you desire?]﴾
﴿So what do you think of the Lord of the worlds?﴾ Its meaning: what do you think of the Lord of the worlds when you meet Him, and what do you expect from Him, when you have done what you have done!

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verses 88–89:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So he cast a glance at the stars﴾ ﴿and said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾

Al-Khalil (ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi) and al-Mubarrad said: the Arabs say of everyone who considers his affair and reflects on what he should do, "he has looked at the stars." This is one view.

The second view: there was a star that rose at that time, and everyone who looked at it, they believed, would be struck by plague. It is said that it was Saturn. So His words, ﴿So he cast a glance at the stars﴾, mean he looked at the star. ﴿And said, "Indeed, I am sick"﴾, meaning: the plague has struck me, according to what you claim. They would flee from the one afflicted with plague with a great flight, believing that it is contagious. This was related by al-Suddi.

The third view: the meaning of His words ﴿So he cast a glance at the stars﴾ is: regarding what the star had decreed for him, that is, what had appeared.

The fourth view: His words ﴿So he cast a glance at the stars﴾ mean: he looked at the stars in the manner in which the astrologers look at them, and he thereby outwitted them concerning his religion. They were astrologers, and they believed that judgments proceed from the stars and events come about through them. So he looked at the stars and said this statement so that they would leave him alone, and by this he could reach their idols with a plot.

It is related from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the knowledge of the stars was true until the sun was held back for Yusha' ibn Nun, whereupon the matter became confused for them. And Allah knows best.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, I am sick﴾, we have already explained it: "sick" means "I will become sick," for every healthy person must fall sick. It was also said: the heart becomes sick because of the ugliness of your deeds. This is one of the three lies which Ibrahim told concerning Allah, and the report about this is well known and authentic, and we have related it.

Some of them said: that was among the figurative uses of speech (ma'arid al-kalam), and it was not an outright lie.

"Then they turned away from him, retreating." That is, they turned away from him and left him.

We have already mentioned that they went out to a festival of theirs. When they had gone out and Ibrahim remained alone, he went to the house of their idols and entered it, and the food was placed before them. He said: "Will you not eat?" This is the meaning of

His words: ﴿Then he turned to their gods﴾, and his words "راغ" (raagha) means: he inclined.

His words: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ This is in the manner of a rebuke against the polytheists, because they had brought the food to them so that they might eat.
His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not speak?﴾ means: "Why do you not talk?" This too is stated in the manner of rebuke.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 93:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So he turned upon them﴾, meaning: he inclined toward them, striking them with a blow, by the right hand.

As for His saying: ﴿by the right hand﴾, there are several opinions on it. One of them is that its meaning is: he struck them with his right hand. The meaning of "striking them" is: he broke them. It is also said "by the right hand," meaning: by strength.

The third opinion: "by the right hand" means: by the oath that had preceded from him, which is the Exalted's saying: ﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 94:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they came hastening toward him﴾. That is: they hurried.

Translation:

And His words: ﴿He said: "Do you worship what you carve?"﴾ That is: what you carve with your own hands.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah created you and what you make﴾ — that is, these idols. So since Allah created them, it is not fitting that you take them as gods. In the verse there is evidence against the Mu'tazila, in that the actions of the servants are created by Allah, may He be exalted, and the proof for this is clear, and it is well known in the books.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ "A structure" means a enclosure (ḥaẓīrah), and it is said: an iwan (a vaulted hall).

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They built a place and made its walls of iron. Its length in the sky was thirty cubits, and its width twenty cubits.

As for His words, ﴿throw him into the blazing fire﴾: al-Jaḥīm is every place in which the fire is great and abundant. It is also said: al-Jaḥīm is fire upon fire, and embers upon embers.

And their saying: ﴿They intended a scheme against him﴾ — their scheme was their intent to burn him with fire. And their saying: ﴿So We made them the lowest﴾ — that is, the ones destroyed. It was also said: "the lowest" in argument, as Ibrahim's proof was against them and prevailed over them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 99:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾

Regarding the story: when Abraham, peace be upon him, was thrown into the fire, he said at the moment he was thrown: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So Allah made the fire cool and safe for him. Ka'b said: "It burned nothing of him except his bonds." And in the story: Nimrod looked down upon him and saw him in a green meadow, with a figure on his right, and that was Jibril, peace be upon him, and on his left was a bed of silk that Allah had sent down to him from Paradise.

As for His words, ﴿"Indeed, I am going to my Lord"﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. One of the two opinions is that he said it after he had come out of the fire, when Allah commanded him to emigrate to the Levant (al-Sham).

The other opinion is that he said this before he was thrown into the fire, and he believed that if he were thrown into the fire he would perish and would not be saved from it; so he said these words: "Indeed, I am going to my Lord."

As for His words, ﴿"He will guide me"﴾, according to this opinion its meaning is: to the path of Paradise. And according to the first opinion, "He will guide me" means: He will direct me to the place to which I was commanded to emigrate.

Translation:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a son] from among the righteous﴾. That is: grant me a righteous son from among the righteous.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 101:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy﴾, meaning: a boy who is forbearing in his youth and knowing in his old age. The verse indicates that he was given the good news that the boy would grow up and live long enough to be described as possessing forbearance (ḥilm) and dignity (waqār).

The scholars differed as to whether this boy was Ismā'īl or Isḥāq.

A group held that it was Isḥāq (peace be upon him), and this is the view of ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Kaʿb, Qatādah and a group of others. Another group held that it was Ismā'īl (peace be upon him), and this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, al-Ḥasan and others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 102:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then when he reached with him the age of exertion﴾. Tha'lab said: al-sa'y (exertion) is walking swiftly. The scholars differed concerning al-sa'y here. Some of them said: it is the work with him, as if he became helping him in his work. It was also said: al-sa'y is toward the mountain. And it is said: "balagha ma'ahu al-sa'y" means: the worship of Allah, the Exalted.

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I sacrifice you"﴾, meaning: I have been commanded to sacrifice you. Ibn 'Abbas said: the dream of the prophets is revelation. And it is said: I saw in a dream what indicates that I have been commanded to sacrifice you.

And His saying: ﴿So see what you think﴾. Hamza recited: "madha tara" (with a damma on the ta'). As for His saying ﴿what you think﴾, it means: what do you think regarding what Allah has commanded? If it is said: how would he consult him regarding what Allah had commanded him, when it is a decisive command which may not be abandoned?

The answer to this is in two respects. One of them: what is meant by it is informing him. The other: he intended to test him in submitting to the decree of Allah.

As for the other recitation, which is His saying ﴿what do you see?﴾, it has two meanings. One of them: "what do you indicate?" And the other: "what do you see of your patience?" This was mentioned by al-Farra'.

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast"﴾. He said that out of submission to the command of his Lord and obedience, and His saying ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast﴾ means: steadfast upon the decree of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 103:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When they had both submitted﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "فَلَمَّا سلما" (fa-lamma salama, "when they had both surrendered").

And His saying: ﴿aslama﴾ means istaslama (they surrendered, submitted completely). Its meaning is that Ibrahim surrendered his son to be slaughtered, and the son surrendered his soul.

And His saying: ﴿and he threw him down upon his forehead﴾, meaning he felled him onto his brow (lit. jabin). The jabha (forehead) lies between the two jabin (temples). The poet said:

(I pierced his side with a spear, so that his shirt was torn; he fell, both hands prostrate, face down.)

And another said:

(He threw him down upon the brow, dust-covered, from him the aorta (manat al-watin) stood out.)

They differed concerning the place where he intended to slaughter him. Whoever says the one sacrificed was Isma'il says it was in Mina; whoever says the one sacrificed was Ishaq says it was in al-Sham (the Levant).

In the tafsir it is related that Isma'il, peace be upon him, said to Ibrahim: "Lay me down on my forehead, so that you do not see my face and have mercy on me, and so that I do not see the blade and panic from it." In the account: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, went out toward the side of Mina, and commanded Isma'il to follow him with the knife and the rope; he took them up and followed him. Then Iblis, may he be cursed, came to Isma'il and said: "Do you know what your father intends for you?" He said: "No." He said: "He intends to slaughter you." He said: "Why?" He said: "He claims that God has commanded him to do it." He said: "He is worthy to be obeyed." Then he came to his mother and whispered likewise; she answered as we have said, meaning: as Isma'il, peace be upon him, had said.

In the tafsir it is also related that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, began to saw but did not cut through. It is narrated that God, exalted is He, placed a plate of copper upon the neck of Isma'il, peace be upon him, so he could not cut. Some have also mentioned that he would cut and it would heal over.

And His saying: ﴿And We called out to him, "O Ibrahim"﴾. If it is asked: where is the response (jawab) to His saying: ﴿So when they had both submitted and he had laid him down upon his forehead﴾?

The answer: its response is His saying ﴿And We called out to him﴾, and the waw is extra (silah). Some of them made the response elided (mahdhuf), and His saying: ﴿And We called out to him, "O Ibrahim"﴾.

Qad saddaqta al-ru'ya (You have indeed fulfilled the vision): that is, you have made the vision true by doing what you were commanded. And His words, ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers﴾: that is, those who affirm the oneness of God (al-muwahhidin).

If it is asked: how did He say "you have fulfilled the vision," when he saw that he was slaughtering [his son] and did not actually slaughter him?

The answer: he did what was within his power of slaughter, and so He made him one who had fulfilled it in this sense. The other answer: the purpose of the command and what was required from it was their submission, this one (Ibrahim) of his son and that one (Isma'il) of his soul. So when both of them did that, He called them those who had fulfilled it.

The scholars differed about Isma'il's age at that time. Some said: he was [thirteen] years old, and others said: he was seven years old.

﴿Indeed, this is surely the manifest trial.﴾ That is, the clear trial. Among them are those who said: it is the manifest blessing, and the blessing lies in the averting of the slaughter from him and the ransom that was sent down to him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 37, verse 107:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: God the Most High sent down to him a ram from Paradise, and it is the same ram that God accepted from Habil (Abel). It is also said: it was a ram that grazed in Paradise for forty autumns. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it was a wild goat (ariwah) from the mountain.

As for His words ﴿great﴾, some said: what is meant is great in body. It was also said: great in reward. Mujahid said: great because it was accepted by God.

In the exegesis it is related that the ram descended to him from the mountain of Mina. He said to Isma'il: "Stand up, for God the Most High has sent its ransom." In the narration it is also said that the ram fled, so Ibrahim pursued it until he caught it. When it reached between the two jamarat, it lay down, and Ibrahim could not bear to carry it, so he slaughtered it right there.
And His saying: ﴿And We left for him among later generations﴾, meaning: We left for him among the later generations a good repute and a fair remembrance.
"And His saying: ﴿Peace be upon Ibrahim﴾ — we have already explained it,"
And His saying: ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾ has already been explained.
And His saying: ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 112:

And His saying: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ Whoever holds that Ishmael was the one who was sacrificed (al-dhabih) argues from this: for [the Qur'an] mentioned the story of the one who was sacrificed in its entirety, and then said: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous,﴾ which indicates that he (the one sacrificed) was other than Isaac. As for whoever holds that the one sacrificed was Isaac, he says regarding this verse: the good news here occurred with the prophethood of Isaac, while the first good news was with his birth and his being granted to [Abraham].

And His saying: ﴿And We blessed him and Isaac﴾, meaning: We blessed Abraham and Isaac. The blessing here is the multiplication of offspring; it is also said that the blessing is the multiplication of prophets among their descendants.

And His saying: ﴿And among their descendants are the one who does good and the one who wrongs himself openly﴾, meaning: the monotheist and the polytheist.
"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly bestowed favour upon Moses and Aaron﴾, meaning: We bestowed blessings upon them."

And His saying: ﴿And We gave them both the clear Book﴾ — that is, the Torah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 139:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers﴾. That is: among the company of Allah's messengers.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ — that is, the ship that is full, filled to capacity.

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿fasahama﴾ means: he cast lots. Its meaning is: he drew lots.

And His words ﴿fa-kana min al-mudhadin﴾ mean: so he was among those who lost the draw. It is also said: among the defeated. One says "dahadat hujjatu fulan" when the argument of so-and-so was refuted, and "adhda Allahu hujjatahu" when God refuted his argument. Al-dahd is the slippery ground. The poet said:

*"Abu Mundhir, you sought loyalty and it frightened you,*
*and you swerved as the camel swerves away from the slippery ground."*

It is related in the tafsir that Yunus, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, warned his people of punishment, and Allah had informed him that He would send the punishment upon them on a certain day. Yunus informed them of this, but they did not believe him. So he left them, and he thought that when Allah sent the punishment He would destroy them, and would not turn it away from them. Allah had told him of the sending of the punishment upon them, but had not told him of their destruction. Then Allah sent the punishment. When they saw it, and it had not yet descended upon them, they went out to the open desert, taking with them the women, the children and the animals, and they separated the mothers from their young. They cried out to Allah with one great cry, sought relief, wept and supplicated. So Allah turned the punishment away from them. When it reached Yunus, peace be upon him, that the punishment had not descended upon them and they had not been destroyed, he went out from the place where he had taken refuge, like a runaway ashamed before his people. He thought that he had made a promise on Allah's behalf, and that its fulfilment had not occurred. So he headed toward the side of the sea.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿abaqa﴾ mean: he went away and distanced himself. It is said: he resembled a runaway slave, so Allah rebuked him for this and tested him by placing him in the belly of the fish, where He imprisoned him.

In the narrative: when he reached the sea, he had with him his wife and two sons. A ship came and he wished to board it with them. He sent his wife ahead onto the ship so that he would board after her. A wave came between him and the ship, and the ship passed on. Then another wave came and seized his elder son, and a wolf came and seized his younger son, and he remained alone and solitary. Then another ship appeared, and he signalled to them to carry him. The ship came and he boarded it and sat in a corner among the people. When the ship had sailed on the sea, it stopped and did not move, and the sea became turbulent, and they feared drowning. The captain of the ship said: "Among you is an ill-omened man," and in another narration: "a sinner." He said: "We must cast him into the sea until the sea calms and we are saved." In another narration he said: "Among you is a runaway slave." Then Yunus, peace be upon him, stood up and said: "I am the sinful servant, and I am the runaway." They said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Yunus son of Matta." They recognised him and said: "We will not cast you away, O Messenger of Allah, but we will cast lots." So they cast lots three times, and the lot fell upon him. It is also narrated that they said: "Let each of us write his name on a piece of wood; whoever's name sinks is the one sought." So the name of Yunus sank among them. Allah inspired a great fish until it approached the ship. They said: when the people of the ship saw it, its mouth gaping open, huge like a mountain, they feared destruction, and the fish kept looking at the people in the ship as if seeking something. Then when Yunus saw this, he threw himself into the water. It is narrated that the people cast him overboard with his consent, and the fish swallowed him and passed on with him. The sea calmed and the ship sailed on.

In some reports: Allah inspired the fish, "I have not made him a provision for you, so beware lest you break one of his bones or scratch his flesh. I have only made your belly a refuge and a place of worship for him."

Concerning the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿So the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. We have already explained the swallowing.

And His saying: ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ means: he had done that for which he was deserving of blame.
Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, i.e., one of those who pray to Allah Almighty and remember Him before the fish swallowed him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 144:

﴿To remain in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ That is: We made the belly of the fish a grave for him, so that he would be gathered from it. It was also said: Had he not been one of those who glorify (Allah) in the belly of the fish, and his glorification being what we mentioned earlier: ﴿Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-Dahhak said: Allah the Exalted rewarded him for his former obedience. And from some of them it is related that he said: Righteous deeds lift up their doer when he stumbles, and take him by the hand when he is thrown down.

And in some reports: When Yunus (peace be upon him) called upon Allah the Exalted in the belly of the fish, the angels said: "A familiar voice from a strange land." So the angels said: "O our Lord, who is it?" He said: "My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the fish."

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that Yunus (peace be upon him) called upon his Lord in the belly of the fish and said: "My God, You brought me out from the houses, concealed me in the seas, and imprisoned me in the belly of the fish. If I have done any righteous deed for You, then relieve me."

He also mentioned: that he met Qarun in the depths of the seas. Qarun heard the voice of Yunus (peace be upon him) and was in severe punishment, so he asked that the punishment be withheld from him until he could ask Yunus. Allah the Exalted ordered the punishment to be withheld from him. Qarun asked Yunus about his cousin Musa, and he said: "He has died." He asked about Harun, and he said: "He died before him." So Qarun said: "Alas for my sorrow!" Allah the Exalted then ordered that the punishment be returned to him until the Day of Resurrection, because he asked about his cousin.

He also mentioned: that the fish travelled with him through the depths of the seas for a distance of six thousand years, and he mentioned that it reached with him the lowest parts of the seventh earths. He heard from the glorification of the pebbles and what is in the bottom of the sea something tremendous. He also mentioned that the sea spoke to him and said: "Where did you want to flee from my Master, O sinful servant?" ﴿To the earth, or to the heaven, or to the seas, or to the mountains?﴾ We have been glorifying Allah the Exalted since He created us, and serving Him, and we fear that He will punish us. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 145:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We cast him onto the open plain while he was ailing﴾. Opinions differ regarding the length of Yunus's stay in the belly of the fish. Ibn Jurayj (and al-Suddi) mentioned that he stayed forty days. Muqatil mentioned that he stayed three days. Al-Dahhak mentioned that he stayed twenty days. ʿAta' mentioned that he stayed seven days. Al-Sha'bi mentioned that he stayed less than a day, and that the fish swallowed him and then spat him out after a few hours.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The fish cast him out, and he was like a young bird (fledgling). In the exegesis it is mentioned that the fish cast him out when his flesh had decayed, his bones had become soft, and he no longer had any strength.

As for his saying ﴿bi-l-ʿarāʾ﴾ (onto the open plain), there are two views. One: that al-ʿarāʾ is the surface of the earth. The other: that it is an empty, open place. This was mentioned by Abu ʿUbayda, who said the poet said:

(And I raised my leg, not fearing its stumbling, / and cast my garments down on the open plain.)

His saying ﴿wa-huwa saqīm﴾ (while he was ailing), i.e., weak. It was also said: in the position of one who is sick.

﴿And We caused a tree of yaqtin to grow over him﴾. Here it is the *dubba'* (gourd) according to all the exegetes. Tha'lab said: every tree that has no stalk and spreads out over the surface of the earth is a *yaqtin*. The *qat'ina* (a single *yaqtin* plant) is well known, and its plural is *qatani*.

Al-Naqqash mentioned that this *dubba'* (gourd) was from the seeds of Paradise, and that it had a thousand leaves on it.

In the story: Yunus sheltered under that tree, and began eating from it and drinking from its water until he grew strong. Then God Most High dried up the tree, and he had slept a sleep, and he awoke, and the tree had dried up; so he grieved intensely, and the heat of the sun struck him, and he began to weep. So God sent Jibril (peace be upon him) to him, and said: "Do you grieve over a tree, and do not grieve over a hundred thousand of your community, who have submitted and turned in repentance to Me?" Then God Most High commanded him to return to his people. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: his prophethood was after God Most High brought him out of the belly of the fish. The more correct view is that he was a prophet before that, and this is indicated by the saying of God Most High: ﴿And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers, when he fled.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿to a hundred thousand or more﴾, al-Farra' said: "Rather, they are more (bal yazidun)." It was also said: "yazidun" (they are more). Al-Mubarrad said: the word "aw" (or) here is in its proper sense, and its meaning is: "or more, according to your estimation and assumption." It is like a man who sees a group of people and says: "These are a thousand," then says: "a thousand or more." So the doubt returns to the one who saw them, not to God Most High. As for the amount of the increase, the most well-known opinion is that it is twenty thousand, and Abu 'Isa mentioned it in his Jami' as a hadith traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

The second opinion: thirty-five thousand. The third opinion: seventy thousand.

As for the town to which he was sent, it is "Nineveh" (Nينوى) in the lands of Mosul.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 148:

His saying: ﴿So they believed, and We let them enjoy for a while﴾ means: until the end of their terms (ājāl).

If it is said: Here He said ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore while he was sick﴾, and in another place He said ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open shore while he was blameworthy﴾, and this indicates that he was not cast out. How then is the reconciliation between the two verses?

The answer to this: God, exalted is He, said in that verse: ﴿he would have been cast onto the open shore while he was blameworthy﴾. That is: had it not been for Our mercy and Our blessing, he would have been cast onto the open shore while blameworthy. But the blessing overtook him, so he was cast out while not blameworthy. And he recited, "aw" (or) meaning bal (rather).

(It appeared like the sun's disc in the brilliance of the forenoon, and its form, or rather you are sweeter in the eye.)

That is: bal (rather) you.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So ask them﴾. Its meaning: ask them. It is a question of rebuke and confrontation. And His saying: ﴿Has your Lord got daughters while they have sons?﴾ means: they assigned daughters to your Lord, and sons to themselves, i.e., they chose this for themselves.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ Its meaning: Did We create the angels as females? ﴿And they were witnesses﴾: We created them as females. They used to claim that the angels are the daughters of God. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: Not all of Quraysh held this view; rather, only some of Quraysh said this, along with a group of the Banu Kinanah, namely the Banu Mudlij.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their own fabrication [ifk] that they say, "Allah has begotten a son," and indeed they are liars﴾. That is, from their lying. And His saying: ﴿They say, "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars﴾, and it is as Allah the Exalted said.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their own fabrication [ifk] that they say, "Allah has begotten a son," and indeed they are liars﴾. That is, from their lying. And His saying: ﴿They say, "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars﴾, and it is as Allah the Exalted said.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 153:

The words of the Most High, ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ mean: Has He chosen daughters over sons? This is an interrogative with the sense of rebuke and reproach. It was also recited as "Isṭafā" (with a kasra on the alif), as a declarative statement, and its meaning is: He has chosen daughters over sons, according to your claim and your saying.
And His words, ﴿What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ mean: how do you claim that God, exalted is He, chose daughters over sons, when you yourselves choose only sons?
"And His saying: ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ meaning: Will you not then take admonition?"
Allah's saying, ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾ That is: a manifest proof.
And His saying: ﴿Then bring your Book, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: a book from yourselves that supports what you have claimed, ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 158:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾. Al-Jinn here are the angels, according to the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun). It is also related from some of them that they are the jinn. Some of the Quraysh had claimed that the angels are the daughters of God, as we have mentioned. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "Then who are their mothers?" They said: "The chieftains of the jinn." This is the meaning of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾.

And His words: ﴿And the jinn have certainly known that they will be brought forward [for judgment]﴾, meaning: they will be brought forward for the reckoning. It was also said: they will be brought forward for punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 37, verse 159:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾. He declared Himself free of what they ascribed to Him by this abominable statement.

And His words: ﴿except the sincere servants of Allah﴾. We have mentioned this before. If it is said: what is the connection (ittisal)?

For his saying (Allah's words): ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾, [and] with His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾. And how is the exception (istithna') valid in this context, when the word illa (except) is for exception?

The answer to this: in the verse there is a transposition (taqdim wa ta'khir, inversion of word order), as if Allah, exalted is He, said: "And the jinn have certainly known that they will be brought forth [to the punishment], except the sincere servants of Allah, for they will not be brought forth," then He said, "Glory be to Allah above what they describe." This is the intended meaning (taqdir) of the verse.
"So indeed you, and what you worship," — that is, the idols.

And His saying: ﴿So you cannot lead anyone astray [against Him]﴾, meaning: you cannot lead anyone astray from God, except those whom God has led astray. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They cannot lead astray anyone except the one for whom God has decreed misguidance." This view is transmitted from al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Dahhak and others.

The poet said:

(So He turned back his plot against him, ... and he was a seducer [fatin] to us)

That is: a misleader (mudill).

Some of them said: "They will not lead astray anyone except the one whom God has written down as entering the Hellfire." It was also said: "except the one whom God has made wretched." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿except one who is destined to burn in the Hellfire﴾.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾. This is a report about the angels, and its meaning is: there is no angel among us but has a known station. In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "There is no place in the heaven where a foot can be placed except that there is an angel standing, or bowing, or prostrating."

It is also said that the station of Jibril is at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), and there is no passing beyond it to its abode.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 177:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard﴾, meaning: it descends upon their courtyard, and its meaning is: the punishment befalls them. And His saying: ﴿then evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾, meaning: evil is the morning of those who were warned of the punishment. It is established that when the Prophet (ﷺ) campaigned against Khaybar and arrived there, he saw the Jews had come out of their fortresses with their baskets and their shovels. When they saw the army, they said: "Muhammad and the army!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God is greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And turn away from them for a while﴾. It has the same meaning as the first [mention], and it is repeated for emphasis.
And His saying: ﴿And see, for they will see﴾ — that is, wait and watch their condition and what their affair will come to; so they will wait for their state and for what will befall them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 37, verse 180:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Majesty, above what they describe﴾. That is: the One possessing majesty (dhu al-'izzah).
"And His saying: ﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾ — meaning: the prophets who were sent to the creation."

And His saying: ﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, according to what we have mentioned. Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Whoever wishes to receive his reward on the Day of Resurrection by the fullest measure, let the last of his words in his assembly be: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe﴾ to the end of the surah."

And in some reports, through the narration of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, it is related: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, when he prayed or when he rose from his assembly, ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe﴾ to the end of the surah."
